analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by an out-of-bounds write in iterateCIPRanks(): `cipEntries[i][numIts + 1] = ranks[i]` (line ~1022) assumes each per-atom CIP entry vector has length at least `numIts+2`. But the vectors are aggressively truncated every loop via `erase(begin()+numIts+2, end())`, and for some malformed molecules from MolDataStream parsing, `longestEntry` can be too short to preserve that index across iterations. This leaves some `cipEntries[i]` with size equal to `numIts+1`, so writing at `[numIts+1]` writes one int past the allocation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger path: fuzzed mol block bytes -> MolDataStreamToMol() -> finishMolProcessing() -> assignStereochemistry() -> assignAtomChiralCodes() -> assignAtomCIPRanks() -> iterateCIPRanks(). Input must produce a molecule that enters CIP ranking loop (`numRanks < numAtoms`) and yields inconsistent/short CIP entry growth for at least one atom (e.g., degenerate/invalid topology from parser), so that after truncation/padding logic a `cipEntries[i]` vector is smaller than expected when `numIts` advances. Then the fixed-index rank write at `numIts+1` causes 4-byte heap OOB write.
